source_records.title: DSpark: Confidence-Scheduled Speculative Decoding with Semi-Autoregressive Generation
source_records.relevance: Defines DSpark's semi-autoregressive draft and confidence-scheduled verification design; supports evaluating ADL only as a backend capability candidate, not as a prompt-level provider feature.

source_records.title: ADL speculative decoding deterministic commit-boundary prototype
source_records.relevance: Existing ADL proof requires target-verified token commit, explicit tokenizer mismatch rejection, and no expansion of tool or side-effect authority.

candidate_rows.acceptance_condition: A serving backend must expose DSpark-style draft generation, target verification, accepted-token counts, fallback counts, and tokenizer compatibility for the same Qwen family.
candidate_rows.reason: Qwen is plausible as a same-family speculative-decoding candidate, but ADL currently has no live DSpark/Qwen draft-verify backend to prove accepted length or throughput.

candidate_rows.acceptance_condition: A serving backend must expose DSpark-style draft generation, target verification, accepted-token counts, fallback counts, and tokenizer compatibility for the same Gemma family.
candidate_rows.reason: Gemma is plausible as a same-family local or hosted candidate, but existing ADL Gemma evidence covers model usefulness, not DSpark-style speculative acceptance or throughput.

candidate_rows.acceptance_condition: None for v0.91.7; cross-family pairings must not be treated as accepted speculative acceleration evidence.
candidate_rows.reason: The ADL speculative-decoding prototype treats tokenizer mismatch as non-proving. Cross-family Qwen/Gemma pairings would widen that risk unless a backend proves tokenizer identity and target-verified commit behavior.

candidate_rows.acceptance_condition: Issue #4654 must run the bounded ephemeral 2xH100 AWS smoke, record teardown, and retain provider/model outcome evidence before this row can be accepted.
candidate_rows.reason: The external DSpark result is specifically tied to the DeepSeek-V4 serving system; ADL should prove that path in #4654 rather than infer it from Qwen/Gemma candidates.

recommendation: Do not claim Qwen or Gemma DSpark acceleration as accepted in v0.91.7 from planning evidence alone. Keep Qwen/Gemma as same-family candidates, reject cross-family Qwen/Gemma pairings, and route actual DeepSeek-V4 DSpark live proof to #4654.
required_next_proof: A same-family Qwen or Gemma backend must expose draft tokens, target verification, accepted-token counts, fallback counts, tokenizer compatibility, latency, and throughput before ADL can accept the row.
Issue #4654 must prove or truthfully block the deepseek-v4-flash-dspark live GPU smoke with Agent Logic AWS account guard and teardown evidence.
The shared provider proof #5026 must consume only rows that have live or accepted blocked dispositions.
authority_rules: Speculative draft tokens remain provisional until target verification accepts them.
Accepted token counts and throughput claims must come from the backend, not prompt-level model text.
Speculative decoding cannot grant tool, mutation, merge, or side-effect authority.
Cross-family tokenizer mismatch is a fail-closed condition unless the backend proves compatibility.
non_claims: does not prove live Qwen DSpark acceleration
does not prove live Gemma DSpark acceleration
does not prove DeepSeek-V4 DSpark availability on AWS
does not claim broad speculative decoding support in ADL provider routing
does not replace #4654 live GPU smoke or #5026 shared provider acceptance proof
